definitions.gloss: rushing about busily; running around in all directions
definitions.explanation: To run about busily from place to place trying to get things done. A four-character idiom (yojijukugo) expressing energetic but hectic activity.

examples.japanese: {東奔西走|とうほんせいそう}する{毎日|まいにち}だ。
examples.english: Every day is spent rushing about.

examples.japanese: {資金集|しきんあつ}めのために{東奔西走|とうほんせいそう}した。
examples.english: I ran around everywhere to raise funds.

examples.japanese: イベントの{準備|じゅんび}で{東奔西走|とうほんせいそう}して、{疲|つか}れ{果|は}てた。
examples.english: I was completely exhausted from rushing around preparing for the event.

notes:
A {四字熟語|よじじゅくご} (four-character compound) meaning to rush about in all directions. Literally: {東|ひがし} (east) + {奔|ほん} (run) + {西|にし} (west) + {走|そう} (run) — "running east and running west."

USAGE:
Used as a する verb: {東奔西走|とうほんせいそう}する. Implies being extremely busy going from place to place to handle various matters. Often used for work-related hustle, fundraising, or event preparation.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {東奔西走|とうほんせいそう}する{毎日|まいにち}: days spent rushing about
- 〜のために{東奔西走|とうほんせいそう}する: to rush around for ~
- {東奔西走|とうほんせいそう}して{疲|つか}れる: to be tired from rushing about

REGISTER:
Fairly literary/formal. More vivid and emphatic than simply saying {忙|いそが}しい (busy). Often appears in written narratives and formal speech.

RELATED WORDS:
- {奔走|ほんそう}する: to run about, to make efforts (two-character version, more common)
- {駆|か}け{回|まわ}る: to run around (everyday equivalent)
